content:
I think we should agree a policy on use of docs#IsAdjoinRoot.

Throughout Mathlib, many ad-hoc isomorphisms between field algebras are constructed. In my view, we should use docs#IsAdjoinRoot instead where possible.

This post is triggered by me seeing #42069 get merged, which defines compAlgEquiv : AdjoinRoot (f.comp g) ≃ₐ[R] AdjoinRoot (g.map (of f) - C (root f)).

I think docs#AdjoinRoot should be viewed as a particular model of the field algebra given by adjoining a root of a polynomial, and all the API should be generically in docs#IsAdjoinRoot. This isn't the case at the moment, but this PR is a step in the wrong direction from that perspective.

If we want to keep putting API into docs#AdjoinRoot, then I think we probably look at removing docs#IsAdjoinRoot and instead just have isomorphisms between eg docs#AdjoinRoot, docs#QuadraticAlgebra, etc.

Relevant people @Aaron Liu @Yaël Dillies @Johan Commelin
(I also think docs#IsAdjoinRoot shouldn't carry data but this is beside the point. I don't want to put effort into refactoring a construct that's not getting made use of.)
Makes sense. Do you think removing AdjoinRoot works? In one of my PR's this was a topic to use IsAdjoinRoot. And unifying those would make it prettier indeed.
We can't remove it - we need a model for IsAdjoinRoot. But we can move its API.
Ah I see, so will AdjoinRoot be kept minimal then?
That's my proposal. I'm not sure what others think, hence this thread.
I like it. Although I also think that it would be good if it didn't carry data. How do you propose that?
I have another thread on this. I think they're separate refractors, unless this one becomes hard to implement without making IsAdjoinRoot into a class (I don't think this will be the case).
https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/287929-mathlib4/topic/Should.20.60PowerBasis.60.20take.20a.20parameter/with/556722342
Btw, if you implement something like IsAdjoinRoot.choose, then you can prove IsAdjoinRoot (IsAdjoinRoot.choose) which would allow you to get rid of AdjoinRoot in principle. Just as a thought.
Does this satisfy your model idea?
However many things require AdjoinRoot currently, like this Polynomial.SplittingFieldAuxAux
No because you need to be able to construct R[X]/(f) at some point. You can't just assume you have an IsAdjoinRoot
But facts about that algebra should IMO always be written generically, ie assuming IsAdjoinRoot

metakuntyyy said:

Btw, if you implement something like IsAdjoinRoot.choose, then you can prove IsAdjoinRoot (IsAdjoinRoot.choose) which would allow you to get rid of AdjoinRoot in principle. Just as a thought.

What do you mean by IsAdjoinRoot.choose? What would be the signature of that theorem?

I know, but that is just a value, if you call it AdjoinRoot or its unfolded definition shouldn't matter.

@Aaron Liu this would be the definition of AdjoinRoot, basically rename AdjoinRoot to IsAdjoinRoot.choose, which gives you the explicit model (Polynomial R ⧸ Ideal.span {f}). It isn't related to Classical.choose, it's just a concrete model that you get by merging those definitions into one.
we definitely still want to keep AdjoinRoot, same as we have both docs#Polynomial.SplittingField and docs#Polynomial.IsSplittingField, both docs#AlgebraicClosure and docs#IsAlgClosure
Do the internals of those constructions matter? Couldn't this just be an implementation detail to an existence proof?
it is sort of an "existence proof" though? we construct a ring satisfying IsAdjoinRoot f for any arbitrary given f.

It could, but I think that's a bad design
In any case I think we're getting off the topic of whether to move more API to IsAdjoinRoot

Yes, there exists an S such that for IsAdjoinRoot S f. Getting model is done via choose. Proving the existence is done via the quotient.
Nevertheless I agree that moving to a Prop based API is a good choice. My main rationale is there should be as few ways to construct essentially the same result.

The different models are good for proving different things
eg module-finiteness and module-freeness can be transferred directly from the quotient construction
QuadraticAlgebra is better for computations
etc
So you still want the concrete models even if you don't care about them

I generally agree with this perspective. In pen and paper mathematics we tend to talk about "the" algebraic completion, "the" splitting field, etc. because we recognize that these properties are unique up to the corresponding isomorphisms. But whenever possible we should really be working with the property itself, instead of any particular object in the isomorphism equivalence class.
I'm reminded of how I tell people to avoid docs#Ordinal.ToType, because any property about it is really a property about all orders of the given order type.
Sometimes you do want the explicit model, particularly when building more complex data on top. But most often you don't.
I think I was too fast with merging #42069. I agree that moving API to IsAdjoinRoot is a good strategy.

I'll make some principled PRs when I have time moving API into IsAdjoinRoot and increasing usage of IsAdjoinRoot downstream. My two concerns are import increases (mitigated by splitting files) and usability (we'll see).
